description: This paper by Alan Grant, Paul Williams, George Shaw, Michelle De Voy and Nick Ward of the General Lighthouse Authorities of the United Kingdom and Ireland (GLAs), presented at the Institute of Navigation International Technical Meeting in San Diego in January 2011, reports GLA investigations into three threats to satellite navigation at sea. Contents: results of GPS jamming trials on GLA vessels, their bridge systems and aids to navigation, where service denial produced hazardously misleading information and failures of radar, gyro-compass and AIS; the effect of a reduced GPS constellation, drawing on 2009 and 2010 US Government Accountability Office forecasts; and space weather, explaining how ionospheric total electron content and phase and amplitude scintillation degrade positions, ahead of the 2013 solar maximum. Coverage: UK and Irish waters. Format and access: a nine-page PDF hosted by the Resilient Navigation and Timing Foundation. Licence and cost: free to read; no licence stated. Caveats: dated 2011 and partly qualitative; trial measurements are summarised, not released. Its failure effects on bridge systems can set consequences of GNSS loss from space weather or jamming in hazard exposure and resilience models of port approaches. It relates to the Blackett review and the GNSS economic impact study in the catalogue.
